_about: Device linking of design 2026-11-15-onboarding-trust §8, with the derivations of §2.3 and the verdict strings and order of §2.4 (the row "Device link"). E is the existing device, N the new one.

Hand-authored from the independent oracle in tools/vector-gen/oracle (Node WebCrypto and @noble; no andvari code). Regenerate with `npm run generate` there; `npm run check` fails on any difference. Secrets, nonces and ephemeral keys are fixed.

derive: linkId = b64url(HKDF(s, "andvari/v2|device-link|id", 16)); macKey = HKDF(s, "andvari/v2|device-link|mac", 32). bundleKey = HKDF(UVK, "andvari/v2|device-link|bundle|" + linkId, 32), envelope AD "andvari/v2|device-link-bundle|" + linkId.

url: https://andvaripass.com/d#v2.<O>.<S>, exactly three parts; parsing as for /l links (white space is space, tab, CR and LF; the fragment with or without its #; canonical base64url; a 32-byte secret; the origin grammar; at most 512 characters). expect.verdict ok or bad_link.

commitN = hexLower(SHA-256("andvari/v2|code-commit|" + b64url(nonceN))); a reveal that does not hash to it is bad_reveal. code = u32be(SHA-256("andvari/v2|device-link|code|" + linkId + "|" + nPub + "|" + b64url(nonceN) + "|" + b64url(nonceE))[0..4]) mod 10^6, six digits. typedCode: the text typed into E (`typed`) against the code N shows (`code`, one of the `code` rows): ok, or code_mismatch, which cancels the link. It is compared as text under the rule of §6.11 that §8.2 step 5 applies here: every ASCII space (U+0020) is removed from `typed`, wherever it stands, and what is left must be exactly six ASCII digits equal to `code`. Nothing else is normalised: the code without its leading zero (five digits, the same number), a tab between the digits and a seventh digit are each code_mismatch. `typed` is to be passed on exactly as the JSON string decodes. The first three typedCode rows are unchanged; the six after them were added on 2026-11-15 with that rule.

macs: all are b64url(HMAC-SHA-256(macKey, inputUtf8)). claim: "andvari/v2|device-link|claim|" + linkId + "|" + nPub + "|" + name + "|" + platform + "|" + commitN, with name the claim's name field as sent. pickup proof: "andvari/v2|device-link|pickup|" + linkId + "|" + nPub; proofHash = hexLower(SHA-256 over the proof's 43 ASCII characters). approve: "andvari/v2|device-link|approve|" + linkId + "|" + hexLower(SHA-256(raw outer)): it covers outer only (FC-3).

claim: E checks the claim it reads back. bad_claim: a field outside its type (nPub a b64_32 that is not a low-order X25519 point, name the name type, platform one of §2.3's values, commitN a hex64, mac a b64_32); then bad_mac. A low-order point is one whose product with every clamped scalar is the all-zero value (RFC 7748 §6.1): after masking the top bit and reducing mod p, as RFC 7748 §5 decodes u, it is 0, 1, p - 1 or one of the two points of order 8; the rows use three canonical encodings from the published list (0, 1 and e0eb7a7c...b800), each under a MAC that is right for its bytes. Changed on 2026-11-15: the three rows npub-low-order-zero, npub-low-order-one and npub-low-order-eight are new, at the end of `claim`; every other row of this file is unchanged. claimChanged: a later poll against the claim E fixed when it drew nonceE. nonceChanged: N is served another nonceE than the first it held.

outer: N's checks before any password prompt, with N's key pair `newDevice`, in this order. bad_mac first (approveMac covers the raw sealed bytes, so it is checked before anything is opened or parsed); outer_unopenable (the seal does not open); bad_outer (not exactly {v, origin, userId, email} with v the number 2, an origin, a uuid and an email that is its own emailNorm, in compact JSON); origin_mismatch (not the origin pinned in step 0). Only on ok may N show the password screen.

bundle: N's checks after the pickup and the unlock, with the account's UVK and identity seed, the session's userId, the served genesis, the pin N made in step 0 ({origin, instanceId}) and `verifiedChain`, the hash at each seq of the card chain N has verified for that origin (after fetching forward). A row names sessionUserId, genesisB64, pin or verifiedChain only where it differs from `bundleDefaults`; plaintextUtf8, where given, is the text sealed in innerB64. The genesis verdicts come first (accountgenesis.json): the genesis is verified when the device unlocks, as at every unlock, before the bundle is touched. Then bundle_unopenable; bad_bundle (the strict decode of §8.3); identity_mismatch (the bundle's userId, identityPub or personalVaultId against the session, the seed-derived key and the verified genesis); pin_mismatch (the bundle's origin, instanceId or card checkpoint against the pin, also when the chain ends below the checkpoint).

Compact JSON, for outer and the bundle: no white space outside strings; strings escape only " and the backslash; numbers in the int or ms text form (2.0, 2e0, 02 and -0 are refused); keys in any order; no key twice at any level.

imports: a bundle contact makes a contact current only where the merged account state holds that userId with the same key hash (SHA-256 over the raw 32 key bytes). checkpoints: a vault or card checkpoint {seq, hash} against the served hashes: ok, withheld or fork (the function graded in vaultlog.json). accountState: a high-water mark of the document's in-blob seq, with hash = SHA-256 over the ASCII bytes of the served sealedState string: a served state below it is a rollback, another hash at the same seq a fork.
The cap of 1,000 entries in contacts or vaults cannot be exercised on its own: 1,001 entries of the smallest form are already more than 65,536 bytes.
The extension links no devices and grades none of these rows, and neither does the web client, which must not run or approve a device link (§13).

Changed on 2026-11-15, fourth batch, with the dot-atom and domain rule of emailNorm (spec 01 §5.5): outer.email and the bundle's email must be emailNorms. One expectation changed: outer row email-with-an-escaped-quote (email a"b@example.com) was ok and is now bad_outer, because a quote is not in the dot-atom; no emailNorm can hold " or a backslash any more, so no valid outer has an escaped character. Two rows are new, each at the end of its section: outer email-in-a-display-name-form (bad_outer) and bundle email-in-a-display-name-form (bad_bundle), both with alice<alice@example.com>. No other row changed.

derive.why: the link secret used throughout this file
31 zero bytes and one 0x01 byte (the lowest secret the key floor accepts; all zeros is refused as a wiped key)

bundleKey.why: the bundle key: from the account's UVK and this link's id
the same UVK and another link: another key

parse.why: a line feed, CR LF and a tab inside
a form feed inside: it is not white space, so it is not removed
a vertical tab at the end
four parts: an invite link is not a device link
O decodes to an origin with a path
O decodes to a plain-http LAN address

reveal.why: the new device reveals the nonce it committed to in its claim
another nonce is revealed: the existing device cancels the link
the existing device's own nonceE is replayed as the reveal

code.why: the code the new device shows and the person types into the existing device
changing one input changes the code: another link
changing one input changes the code: another nPub (a swapped claim)
changing one input changes the code: another nonceN
changing one input changes the code: another nonceE
changing one input changes the code: the two nonces swapped
a code below 100000 keeps its leading zero

typedCode.why: the six digits typed into the existing device are the code
one digit off: the link is cancelled
the code as the new device shows it, with one space in the middle: every ASCII space (U+0020) is removed before the comparison (the text rule of §6.11, which §8.2 step 5 applies here)
one space in front of the six digits and one after them: spaces are removed wherever they stand
a code that starts with 0 (the last row of `code`), typed in full, its leading zero included
the same code typed without its leading zero: five digits, the same number and not the same text. The comparison is on text, not on numbers, so this is a mismatch and the link is cancelled
a tab (U+0009) between the third and fourth digits: only the ASCII space is removed, and nothing else is normalised
the six digits of the code and then a seventh: what is left once the spaces are removed must be exactly six digits, and the first six are not taken on their own

claim.why: the claim MAC: nPub and commitN as their text, name as the claim's name field (base64url) as sent
claim.name: UGl4ZWwgOQ

pickup.why: the pickup proof, and proofHash = hexLower(SHA-256 over the 43 ASCII characters of the proof)

approve.why: the approve MAC covers `outer` only: the lowercase hex SHA-256 of the raw sealed bytes

claim.name: valid
claim.why: The claim the server stored, with a MAC only someone holding the link secret can make.

claim.name: npub-swapped
claim.why: The server swapped in its own nPub and kept the MAC.

claim.name: commit-changed
claim.why: commitN was replaced by the commitment to another nonce.

claim.name: mac-of-another-link
claim.why: A MAC made with another link's key.

claim.name: name-is-not-a-name
claim.why: name holds U+202E, which the name type refuses, though the MAC over it is right.

claim.name: name-is-plain-text
claim.why: name is the text itself, not its base64url.

claim.name: name-of-65-bytes
claim.why: name decodes to 65 bytes; the name type allows 1 to 64.

claim.name: platform-unknown
claim.why: platform is not one of §2.3's values.

claim.name: mac-padded
claim.why: mac is not a b64_32 (it is padded).

claim.name: order-claim-before-mac
claim.why: An unknown platform and a wrong MAC: bad_claim comes first.

claim.name: npub-low-order-zero
claim.why: nPub is the all-zero point (u = 0, of order 2), a low-order X25519 point: every key agreement with it gives the all-zero value, so whatever outer is sealed to it is no secret. The MAC over these bytes is right.

claim.name: npub-low-order-one
claim.why: nPub is u = 1 (01 then 31 zero bytes), a point of order 4: low-order. The MAC over these bytes is right.

claim.name: npub-low-order-eight
claim.why: nPub is e0eb7a7c3b41b8ae1656e3faf19fc46ada098deb9c32b1fd866205165f49b800, a point of order 8 from the published list: low-order although its bytes look like any key, so a check for 0 and 1 alone does not catch it. The MAC over these bytes is right.

claimChanged.why: a later poll shows the same claim
a later poll shows another nPub than the claim the existing device fixed when it drew nonceE: the link is cancelled
a later poll shows another name than the claim the existing device fixed when it drew nonceE: the link is cancelled
a later poll shows another platform than the claim the existing device fixed when it drew nonceE: the link is cancelled
a later poll shows another commitN than the claim the existing device fixed when it drew nonceE: the link is cancelled

nonceChanged.why: the poll serves the nonceE the new device already holds
a different nonceE is served after the first: the link is cancelled

bundle.why: A bundle of exactly 65536 bytes, with several hundred contact checkpoints. This row gives the plaintext length and the entry counts in place of the decoded bundle.

bundle.name: user-id-is-not-the-sessions
bundle.why: The bundle names another userId than the session the pickup returned.

bundle.why: The bundle's identityPub is not the key derived from the unlocked seed.

bundle.name: personal-vault-is-not-the-genesis
bundle.why: The bundle's personalVaultId is not the one the verified genesis names.

bundle.name: genesis-signed-by-another-account
bundle.why: The bundle is fine, but the genesis served with the account keys does not verify: a genesis verdict.

bundle.name: genesis-of-another-user
bundle.why: The genesis is signed by this account's key but names another userId than the session: a genesis verdict.

bundle.name: genesis-truncated
bundle.why: The served genesis is 60 bytes of a frame: a genesis verdict from the parse.

bundle.name: genesis-of-another-instance
bundle.why: The genesis names another instance than the pinned card: a genesis verdict.

bundle.name: bundle-origin-is-not-the-pin
bundle.why: T2-B1: the bundle's origin is not the origin this device pinned in step 0. It signs out, removes that pin and shows "This isn't the server your other device uses. Nothing was linked."

bundle.name: bundle-instance-is-not-the-pin
bundle.why: The bundle's instanceId is not the pinned card's.

bundle.name: bundle-card-is-another-hash
bundle.why: The bundle's card checkpoint names another hash at seq 2 than this device's verified chain.

bundle.name: bundle-card-is-ahead-of-the-chain
bundle.why: The checkpoint is card 5; after fetching forward this device's chain still ends at card 2.

bundle.name: order-decode-before-identity
bundle.why: An extra key and another userId: bad_bundle comes first.

bundle.name: order-identity-before-pin
bundle.why: Another userId and another origin: identity_mismatch comes first.

bundle.name: order-genesis-before-pin
bundle.why: A genesis that does not verify and a bundle for another origin: the genesis verdict comes first.

bundle.name: order-genesis-before-unopenable
bundle.why: A genesis that does not verify and an inner from another link. The genesis is verified at the unlock, before the bundle is touched: its verdict comes first.

bundle.name: order-genesis-before-decode
bundle.why: A genesis that names another instance and a bundle with an extra key: the genesis verdict comes first.

bundle.name: order-genesis-before-identity
bundle.why: A genesis that does not verify and a bundle that names another userId: the genesis verdict comes first.

bundle.name: order-genesis-before-identity-key
bundle.why: A genesis that names another instance and a bundle whose identityPub is not the seed's: the genesis verdict comes first.

bundle.name: email-in-a-display-name-form
bundle.why: email is alice<alice@example.com>: lower case, one @, printable ASCII, but not a dot-atom local part, so it is not an emailNorm (spec 01 §5.5).

currency.why: The bundle confers currency, never contacts. bob is in the merged account state with the same key hash: current. carol is there with ANOTHER key: not current. dave is in the bundle but not in the account state: not a contact at all.

checkpoints.why: a vault or card checkpoint against a served chain that holds it and goes on
the served chain ends below the checkpoint: withholding
the served chain has another hash at the checkpoint's seq: a fork

accountState.why: the served state is the one the bundle named: the same in-blob seq and the same hash over the sealedState string
a served state below the checkpoint: a rollback, kept out
another blob at the same in-blob seq: a fork
